title: Prakrama 1, Sarga 3. Narada's Inquiry
html:
Narada goes to Vaikuntha; the vision of Vaikuntha and of Krishna; Narada pleads for the world perishing in Kali; the Lord agrees to descend

Verse 1

कलेः प्रथमसन्ध्यायां निमग्नेयं वसुन्धरा।
सर्वेषां पापदग्धानां हरिनामरसायनः॥१॥

kaleḥ prathamasandhyāyāṁ nimagneyaṁ vasundharā|
sarveṣāṁ pāpadagdhānāṁ harināmarasāyanaḥ||1||

kaleh — of Kali; prathama-sandhyayam — in the first twilight (opening period); nimagna — is sunk; iyam — this; vasundhara — earth; sarvesham — for all; papa-dagdhanam — scorched by sin; hari-nama-rasayanah — the elixir of Hari's name.

1"'In the first twilight of Kali1 this earth has sunk (into sin). For all who are scorched by sin, the name of Hari is the healing elixir;

Verse 2

तारकोऽयं भवत्येव वैष्णवद्वेषिणं विना।
आत्मसम्भाविता ये च ये च वैष्णवनिन्दकाः॥२॥

tārako'yaṁ bhavatyeva vaiṣṇavadveṣiṇaṁ vinā|
ātmasambhāvitā ye ca ye ca vaiṣṇavanindakāḥ||2||

tarakah — a deliverer; ayam — it; bhavati eva — surely becomes; vaishnava-dveshinam — one who hates Vaishnavas; vina — except; atma-sambhavitah — self-conceited; ye — who; cha — and; ye — who; cha — and; vaishnava-nindakah — revilers of Vaishnavas.

2it surely delivers everyone except those who hate the Vaishnavas — the self-conceited and the revilers of Vaishnavas.

Verse 3

ये कृष्णनाम्नि देहेषु निन्देयुर्मन्दबुद्धयः।
तेऽनित्या इति वक्ष्यन्ते तेषां निरय एव हि॥३॥

ye kṛṣṇanāmni deheṣu nindeyurmandabuddhayaḥ|
te'nityā iti vakṣyante teṣāṁ niraya eva hi||3||

ye — who; krishna-namni — Krishna's name; deheshu — (his) forms; nindeyuh — would revile; manda-buddhayah — the dull-witted; te — they; anityah — non-eternal; iti — thus; vakshyante — will say; tesham — for them; nirayah — hell; eva hi — alone.

3But those dull-witted ones who would revile the name of Krishna and His forms, calling them non-eternal2 — for them there is only hell.

Verse 4

अत्र किं स्यादुपायोऽयमिति निश्चित्य शुद्धधीः।
वैकुण्ठाख्यं परं धाम जगाम करुणानिधिः॥४॥

atra kiṁ syādupāyo'yamiti niścitya śuddhadhīḥ|
vaikuṇṭhākhyaṁ paraṁ dhāma jagāma karuṇānidhiḥ||4||

atra — here; kim — what; syat — could be; upayah — the remedy; ayam — this; iti — thus; nishchitya — having considered; shuddha-dhih — pure of mind; vaikuntha-akhyam — called Vaikuntha; param — the supreme; dhama — abode; jagama — went; karuna-nidhih — the treasury of compassion.

4What remedy can there be for this?' Having pondered thus, the sage, pure of mind, a treasury of compassion, went to the supreme abode called Vaikuntha.

Verse 5

अथ त्रिवेदीपरिगीयमानं
ददर्श वैकुण्ठमखण्डधिष्ण्यम्।
स्वतेजसा ध्वस्तरजःसमूहं
दिशां दशामाप गुणात्परां मुनिः॥५॥

atha trivedīparigīyamānaṁ
dadarśa vaikuṇṭhamakhaṇḍadhiṣṇyam|
svatejasā dhvastarajaḥsamūhaṁ
diśāṁ daśāmāpa guṇātparāṁ muniḥ||5||

atha — then; tri-vedi-parigiyamanam — sung by the three Vedas; dadarsha — saw; vaikuntham — Vaikuntha; akhanda-dhishnyam — the undivided abode; sva-tejasa — by its own radiance; dhvasta-rajah-samuham — that has dispelled the dust (rajas); disham — of the quarters; dasham — a state; apa — attained; gunat — the gunas; param — beyond; munih — the sage.

5And the sage beheld Vaikuntha, the undivided abode sung by the three Vedas, which by its own radiance has scattered all the dust (of rajas) from every quarter; and he attained a state beyond the gunas.

Verse 6

मधुव्रतानां निवहैर्हरेर्यशः
प्रगीयमानं कमलावलीषु।
विराजितं रत्नतटाभिराम-
वापीभिरामुक्तलतासुगन्धिभिः॥६॥

madhuvratānāṁ nivahairhareryaśaḥ
pragīyamānaṁ kamalāvalīṣu|
virājitaṁ ratnataṭābhirāma-
vāpībhirāmuktalatāsugandhibhiḥ||6||

madhu-vratanam — of bees; nivahaih — by swarms; hareh — Hari's; yashah — fame; pragiyamanam — being sung; kamala-avalishu — among rows of lotuses; virajitam — adorned; ratna-tata-abhirama-vapibhih — with ponds lovely with jewelled banks; amukta-lata-sugandhibhih — fragrant with hanging creepers.

6There swarms of bees sing Hari's fame among rows of lotuses; it is adorned with ponds lovely with jewelled banks and fragrant with hanging creepers.

Verse 7

माणिक्यगेहैर्वलभीभिरन्वितं
गजेन्द्रमुक्तावलिभूषिताभिः।
सार्वर्तवैः शाखिभिरन्वितं खगै-
र्विकूजितं चन्द्रशिलापथाढ्यम्॥७॥

māṇikyagehairvalabhībhiranvitaṁ
gajendramuktāvalibhūṣitābhiḥ|
sārvartavaiḥ śākhibhiranvitaṁ khagai-
rvikūjitaṁ candraśilāpathāḍhyam||7||

manikya-gehaih — with ruby houses; valabhibhih — with turrets; anvitam — furnished; gajendra-mukta-avali-bhushitabhih — adorned with strings of pearls from lordly elephants; sarvartavaih — (bearing) in all seasons; shakhibhih — with trees; anvitam — furnished; khagaih — by birds; vikujitam — filled with song; chandra-shila-patha-adhyam — rich in paths of moonstone.

7There are ruby houses with turrets adorned with strings of pearls from the heads of lordly elephants3; there are trees that bear fruit in every season; there birds fill the air with song, and paths of moonstone abound.

Verse 8

तत्र श्रिया जुष्टमजं पुरातनं
लसत्किरीटद्युतिरञ्जितालकम्।
विकासिदिव्याब्जजितेक्षणं लसत्-
सुधाकराराधितसन्मुखोल्लसम्॥८॥

tatra śriyā juṣṭamajaṁ purātanaṁ
lasatkirīṭadyutirañjitālakam|
vikāsidivyābjajitekṣaṇaṁ lasat-
sudhākarārādhitasanmukhollasam||8||

tatra — there; shriya — by Shri (Lakshmi); jushtam — attended; ajam — the unborn; puratanam — the primeval; lasat-kirita-dyuti-ranjita-alakam — whose locks were lit by the radiance of a gleaming crown; vikasi-divya-abja-jita-ikshanam — whose eyes surpassed blooming celestial lotuses; lasat — shining; sudhakara-aradhita-san-mukha-ullasam — radiant with a fair face worshipped by the moon.

8There he saw the Unborn, the Primeval One, whom Shri attends: His locks are lit by the radiance of a gleaming crown, His eyes outshine blooming celestial lotuses, and His fair, shining face is worshipped by the moon itself;

Verse 9

लसन्महाकुण्डलगण्डशोभितं
सुकम्बुकण्ठं कनकोज्ज्वलांशुकम्।
कृष्णं चतुर्भिः परिघोपमैर्भुजै-
र्नीलाद्रिशृङ्गं सुरपादपैरिव॥९॥

lasanmahākuṇḍalagaṇḍaśobhitaṁ
sukambukaṇṭhaṁ kanakojjvalāṁśukam|
kṛṣṇaṁ caturbhiḥ parighopamairbhujai-
rnīlādriśṛṅgaṁ surapādapairiva||9||

lasan-maha-kundala-ganda-shobhitam — whose cheeks were graced by gleaming great earrings; su-kambu-kantham — with a fine conch-like neck; kanaka-ujjvala-amshukam — in garments bright as gold; krishnam — Krishna; chaturbhih — with four; parigha-upamaih — like door-bars; bhujaih — arms; nila-adri-shringam — the peak of a blue mountain; sura-padapaih — with trees of the gods (wish-fulfilling trees); iva — like.

9great gleaming earrings grace His cheeks, His neck is fine as a conch, His garments shine like gold — Krishna, whose four arms are like door-bars: He was like a blue mountain peak with wish-fulfilling trees.

Verse 10

विराजमानं कनकाङ्गदादिभि-
र्मुक्तावलीभिर्वरहेमसूत्रैः।
सकिङ्किणीजालनिबद्धचेलो-
ल्लसन्नितम्बं वरपादपङ्कजम्॥१०॥

virājamānaṁ kanakāṅgadādibhi-
rmuktāvalībhirvarahemasūtraiḥ|
sakiṅkiṇījālanibaddhacelo-
llasannitambaṁ varapādapaṅkajam||10||

virajamanam — resplendent; kanaka-angada-adibhih — with golden armlets and the like; mukta-avalibhih — with strings of pearls; vara-hema-sutraih — with fine golden cords; sa-kinkini-jala-nibaddha-chela-ullasan-nitambam — whose hips shone with a cloth bound by a net of little bells; vara-pada-pankajam — with beautiful lotus feet.

10He was resplendent with golden armlets and other ornaments, with strings of pearls and fine golden cords; on His hips shone a cloth bound with a net of little bells, and His feet were lovely lotuses.

Verse 11

तदीयपादाब्जमनोज्ञगन्ध-
माघ्राय हर्षाश्रुतनूरुहोद्गमैः।
विसंज्ञ एवाशु पपात भूमौ
स दण्डवत्कृष्णसमीपतो मुनिः॥११॥

tadīyapādābjamanojñagandha-
māghrāya harṣāśrutanūruhodgamaiḥ|
visaṁjña evāśu papāta bhūmau
sa daṇḍavatkṛṣṇasamīpato muniḥ||11||

tadiya-pada-abja-manojna-gandham — the charming fragrance of his lotus feet; aghraya — having inhaled; harsha-ashru-tanu-ruha-udgamaih — with tears of joy and bristling hair; visamjnah — senseless; eva — as if; ashu — at once; papata — fell; bhumau — on the ground; sah — he; danda-vat — like a rod; krishna-samipatah — near Krishna; munih — the sage.

11Inhaling the enchanting fragrance of His lotus feet, the sage, with tears of joy and his hair standing on end, at once fell to the ground near Krishna, stretched out like a rod, as if senseless.

Verse 12

ततः प्रसार्याशु करं कृतज्ञो
रत्नाङ्गुरीभिन्ननखप्रभं प्रभुः।
मुदा स्पृशन्मूर्ध्नि मुनेर्मनोहरं
बभाष ईषत्स्मितशोभिताननः॥१२॥

tataḥ prasāryāśu karaṁ kṛtajño
ratnāṅgurībhinnanakhaprabhaṁ prabhuḥ|
mudā spṛśanmūrdhni munermanoharaṁ
babhāṣa īṣatsmitaśobhitānanaḥ||12||

tatah — then; prasarya — stretching out; ashu — at once; karam — his hand; kritajnah — grateful; ratna-anguri-bhinna-nakha-prabham — its nail-radiance variegated by jewelled rings; prabhuh — the Lord; muda — joyfully; sprishan — touching; murdhni — on the head; muneh — of the sage; manoharam — charmingly; babhasha — spoke; ishat-smita-shobhita-ananah — his face graced by a gentle smile.

12Then the grateful Lord at once stretched out His hand, the radiance of its nails mingling with the gleam of jewelled rings, joyfully touched the sage's head and, with a gentle smile on His face, spoke enchantingly:

Verse 13

स्वायम्भुवोत्तिष्ठ मुने महात्मन्
यन्नो वदस्यद्य करोमि तत्ते।
ममैव कालोऽयमुपागतः स्वयं
युगेषु धर्माचरणाय धर्मिणाम्॥१३॥

svāyambhuvottiṣṭha mune mahātman
yanno vadasyadya karomi tatte|
mamaiva kālo'yamupāgataḥ svayaṁ
yugeṣu dharmācaraṇāya dharmiṇām||13||

svayambhuva — O son of the Self-born (Brahma); uttishtha — rise; mune — O sage; maha-atman — O great soul; yat — what; nah — to us; vadasi — you say; adya — today; karomi — I do; tat — that; te — for you; mama — my; eva — indeed; kalah — time; ayam — this; upagatah — has come; svayam — of itself; yugeshu — in the ages; dharma-acharanaya — for the practice of dharma; dharminam — of the righteous.

13'Rise, O son of the Self-born4, O sage, O great soul! Whatever you tell Me today, that I shall do for you. For My time has come of itself — the time when, in the ages, the righteous must practise dharma.'

Verse 14

ततः समुत्थाप्य महर्षिसत्तमं
महत्तमैकान्तपरायणो हरिः।
समादिदेशासनमाशु तस्मै
तस्मिन्निविष्टो मुनिराज्ञया हरेः॥१४॥

tataḥ samutthāpya maharṣisattamaṁ
mahattamaikāntaparāyaṇo hariḥ|
samādideśāsanamāśu tasmai
tasminniviṣṭo munirājñayā hareḥ||14||

tatah — then; samutthapya — raising; maharshi-sattamam — the best of the great rishis; mahattama-ekanta-parayanah — wholly devoted to the greatest souls; harih — Hari; samadidesha — indicated; asanam — a seat; ashu — at once; tasmai — to him; tasmin — on it; nivishtah — sat; munih — the sage; ajnaya — at the command; hareh — of Hari.

14Then Hari, wholly devoted to the greatest souls, raised up the best of the great rishis and at once showed him to a seat; and at Hari's bidding the sage sat down.

Verse 15

अथान्वपृच्छद्भगवान्मुने कथं
सम्प्राप्तवान्मामिह किं तवेप्सितम्।
पूर्णस्य कार्यं करवाणि साधो
परोपकाराय महद्विचेष्टितम्॥१५॥

athānvapṛcchadbhagavānmune kathaṁ
samprāptavānmāmiha kiṁ tavepsitam|
pūrṇasya kāryaṁ karavāṇi sādho
paropakārāya mahadviceṣṭitam||15||

atha — then; anvaprichchhat — asked; bhagavan — Bhagavan; mune — O sage; katham — how (why); sampraptavan — have come; mam — to me; iha — here; kim — what; tava — your; ipsitam — wish; purnasya — (though I am) complete; karyam — the task; karavani — let me do; sadho — O holy one; para-upakaraya — for the good of others; mahad-vicheshtitam — the deeds of the great.

15Then Bhagavan asked: 'O sage, why have you come here to Me? What is your wish? Though I am complete, let Me do your task, O holy one: the great exert themselves for the good of others.'

Verse 16

इत्थं सतोयाम्बुदतुल्यघोषं
वचोऽमृतं कृष्णदयामृताब्धेः।
उवाच पूर्णस्मितवीक्षया हरे-
र्नमामि लोकान्परिपाहि दुःखितान्॥१६॥

itthaṁ satoyāmbudatulyaghoṣaṁ
vaco'mṛtaṁ kṛṣṇadayāmṛtābdheḥ|
uvāca pūrṇasmitavīkṣayā hare-
rnamāmi lokānparipāhi duḥkhitān||16||

ittham — such (was); sa-toya-ambuda-tulya-ghosham — resonant as a rain-laden cloud; vachah — speech; amritam — nectar; krishna-daya-amrita-abdheh — of Krishna, the ocean of the nectar of mercy; uvacha — said; purna-smita-vikshaya — under the glance full of smiles; hareh — of Hari; namami — I bow; lokan — the worlds; paripahi — protect; duhkhitan — suffering.

16Such were the nectarean words of Krishna, the ocean of the nectar of mercy, resonant as a rain-laden cloud. And under Hari's glance, full of smiles, the sage said: 'I bow to You! Protect the suffering worlds!

Verse 17

क्षितिः क्षिणोत्यद्य समाकुला विभो
जनस्य पापौघयुतस्य धारणात्।
जनाश्च सर्वे कलिकालदष्टाः
पापे रतास्त्यक्तभवत्प्रसङ्गाः॥१७॥

kṣitiḥ kṣiṇotyadya samākulā vibho
janasya pāpaughayutasya dhāraṇāt|
janāśca sarve kalikāladaṣṭāḥ
pāpe ratāstyaktabhavatprasaṅgāḥ||17||

kshitih — the earth; kshinoti — is wasting away; adya — now; samakula — distressed; vibho — O mighty one; janasya — of people; papa-augha-yutasya — laden with floods of sin; dharanat — from bearing; janah — people; cha — and; sarve — all; kali-kala-dashtah — bitten by the time of Kali; pape — in sin; ratah — delighting; tyakta-bhavat-prasangah — having abandoned talk of you.

17Now, O mighty Lord, the earth is wasting away in distress under the weight of people laden with floods of sin. All the people, bitten by the time of Kali, delight in sin and have abandoned talk of You.

Verse 18

तान्पाहि नाथ त्वदृते न तेषा-
मन्योऽस्ति पाता निरयात्तु सद्गतिः।
एवं विचार्य कुरु सर्वलोक-
नाथ स्वयं सद्गतिरीश नान्यः॥१८॥

tānpāhi nātha tvadṛte na teṣā-
manyo'sti pātā nirayāttu sadgatiḥ|
evaṁ vicārya kuru sarvaloka-
nātha svayaṁ sadgatirīśa nānyaḥ||18||

tan — them; pahi — protect; natha — O master; tvat-rite — apart from you; na — not; tesham — for them; anyah — another; asti — is; pata — protector; nirayat — from hell; tu — indeed; sat-gatih — good refuge; evam — thus; vicharya — having considered; kuru — act; sarva-loka-natha — O lord of all worlds; svayam — yourself; sat-gatih — the good refuge; isha — O Lord; na — not; anyah — another.

18Protect them, O Master: apart from You they have no other protector from hell, no other good refuge. Consider this and act, O Lord of all worlds: You Yourself are the good refuge, O Lord, and no other.'

Verse 19

इत्थं समाकर्ण्य मुनेर्वचो हरि-
र्विदन्नपि प्राह किमाचरिष्ये।
केनाप्युपायेन भवेद्धि शान्ति-
स्तद्ब्रूहि तं प्राह पुनः स्वभूसुतः॥१९॥

itthaṁ samākarṇya munervaco hari-
rvidannapi prāha kimācariṣye|
kenāpyupāyena bhaveddhi śānti-
stadbrūhi taṁ prāha punaḥ svabhūsutaḥ||19||

ittham — such; samakarnya — having heard; muneh — of the sage; vachah — words; harih — Hari; vidan — knowing; api — though; praha — said; kim — what; acharishye — shall I do; kena api — by what; upayena — means; bhavet — may come; hi — indeed; shantih — peace; tat — that; bruhi — tell; tam — to him; praha — said; punah — again; svabhu-sutah — the son of the Self-born.

19Having heard these words of the sage, Hari, though He knew all, said: 'What shall I do? By what means can peace come about? Tell Me.' And the son of the Self-born spoke to Him again:

Verse 20

स्वयं सुशीतः शतचन्द्रमा यथा
भूदेववंशेऽप्यवतीर्य सत्कुले।
वात्स्ये जगन्नाथसुतेति विश्रुतिं
समाप्नुहि त्वं कुरु शं धरण्याः॥२०॥

svayaṁ suśītaḥ śatacandramā yathā
bhūdevavaṁśe'pyavatīrya satkule|
vātsye jagannāthasuteti viśrutiṁ
samāpnuhi tvaṁ kuru śaṁ dharaṇyāḥ||20||

svayam — yourself; su-shitah — cooling; shata-chandrama — a hundred moons; yatha — like; bhu-deva-vamshe — in a lineage of brahmanas ("gods of the earth"); api — indeed; avatirya — descending; sat-kule — in a good family; vatsye — of the Vatsya line; jagannatha-suta — "son of Jagannatha"; iti — thus; vishrutim — renown; samapnuhi — attain; tvam — you; kuru — make; sham — welfare; dharanyah — of the earth.

20'Descend Yourself, cooling as a hundred moons, into a good family of the brahmana race, of the Vatsya line5; win renown as "the son of Jagannatha," and bring welfare to the earth.

Verse 21

रामादिरूपैर्भगवन्कृतं हि य-
त्पापात्मनां राक्षसदानवानाम्।
वधादिकं कर्म न चेह कार्यं
मनो नराणां परिशोधयस्व॥२१॥

rāmādirūpairbhagavankṛtaṁ hi ya-
tpāpātmanāṁ rākṣasadānavānām|
vadhādikaṁ karma na ceha kāryaṁ
mano narāṇāṁ pariśodhayasva||21||

rama-adi-rupaih — in the forms of Rama and others; bhagavan — O Bhagavan; kritam — done; hi — indeed; yat — which; papa-atmanam — of the sinful; rakshasa-danavanam — of Rakshasas and Danavas; vadha-adikam — slaying and the like; karma — the deed; na — not; cha — and; iha — here; karyam — to be done; manah — the mind; naranam — of men; parishodhayasva — purify.

21What You did, O Bhagavan, in the forms of Rama and others — the slaying of sinful Rakshasas and Danavas and the like — is not to be done here: purify the minds of men.

Verse 22

तानासुरं भावमुपागतान्हि
यदा हनिष्ये क्व तदास्ति लोकः।
एवं व्यवस्य स्वधियात्मनो यशः
प्रख्याहि लोकाः सुखिनो भवन्तु॥२२॥

tānāsuraṁ bhāvamupāgatānhi
yadā haniṣye kva tadāsti lokaḥ|
evaṁ vyavasya svadhiyātmano yaśaḥ
prakhyāhi lokāḥ sukhino bhavantu||22||

tan — them; asuram — demoniac; bhavam — state; upagatan — who have entered; hi — indeed; yada — if; hanishye — I kill; kva — where; tada — then; asti — is; lokah — the world; evam — thus; vyavasya — resolving; sva-dhiya — by your own understanding; atmanah — your own; yashah — glory; prakhyahi — make known; lokah — people; sukhinah — happy; bhavantu — may become.

22"If I slay those who have fallen into the demoniac state, where then will the world be?" — resolving thus in Your own mind, make Your glory known, and may the people be happy.

Verse 23

तत्रैव रुद्रेण मुनिप्रवीराः
कर्तुं हि साहाय्यमवातरिष्यन्।
तथेति तं प्राह हरिः सुरर्षिं
सोऽपि प्रणम्याशु जगाम हृष्टः॥२३॥

tatraiva rudreṇa munipravīrāḥ
kartuṁ hi sāhāyyamavātariṣyan|
tatheti taṁ prāha hariḥ surarṣiṁ
so'pi praṇamyāśu jagāma hṛṣṭaḥ||23||

tatra eva — there too; rudrena — with Rudra; muni-pravirah — the foremost of sages; kartum — to give; hi — indeed; sahayyam — help; avatarishyan — would descend; tatha — so be it; iti — thus; tam — to him; praha — said; harih — Hari; sura-rshim — to the divine rishi; sah — he; api — too; pranamya — bowing; ashu — at once; jagama — went; hrishtah — joyful.

23And there too, together with Rudra, the foremost of sages will descend to help You'6. 'So be it,' Hari said to the divine rishi; and he, bowing, at once departed joyfully."

Thus ends the third sarga, "Narada's Inquiry" (Narada-prashna), of the first prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charita."

✦

Notes

  1. The "twilight" (sandhya) is the opening period of a yuga; the Kali age has only just begun.
  2. The Lord's name and form are eternal and not material; to call them non-eternal is an offence.
  3. According to poetic convention, pearls form in the heads of lordly elephants.
  4. Narada is the son of Brahma, the Self-born (Svayambhu).
  5. Vatsya is the brahmana clan (gotra) to which Jagannatha Mishra belonged.
  6. Which gods and sages descended together with the Lord is told in the next sarga.
